A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same emotional-support framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original ESConv data analysis, model-training and dialogue-simulation results, ablations, and expert assessments, including additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds human evaluation of the seeker simulator, new baseline comparisons, target-reinforcement measurements, and Cactus-based training experiments.

M1.justification: The original Reddit method remains, but the added Cactus adaptation omits DPO when training the reference generator because Cactus lacks branching replies (Appendix J.1). This changes one training stage without redesigning the three-component framework. Expanded descriptions of reference-use reasoning already match v1's appendix prompt.

E1.justification: V2 adds Cactus CBT counseling dialogues as an alternative training source, AnnoMI real counseling responses for simulator evaluation, and evaluation on the SemEval-2023 Task 4 value-classification test set (Appendices B, E, and J). These extend the represented data and evaluation tasks beyond v1's actual dataset usage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Llama-Reddit, Ask-an-Expert, ESCoT, and PPDPP to the evaluated supporter comparators, also extending the appendix comparisons. V1 cited some of these methods but did not include them in these experiments. Appendix B.1 additionally compares the value classifier against binary and probability-based GPT-4o-mini predictions.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a 200-dialogue, 16-evaluator naturalness study; target-success measurement over one to three future turns, conditional on a positive seeker response; and Cactus training and simulation configurations (Appendices E.3, I, and J). Figure 2 also changes its reported aggregation from per-turn probabilities to four-turn counts. The original 120-persona, 20-turn evaluation remains.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether intended target values appear in subsequent responses, whether simulator responses seem natural to humans, and whether training transfers to a non-Reddit source (Table 4, Figure 4, and Section 6.4.4). The original component ablations, DPO sensitivity experiments, self-disclosure analyses, and low-scoring-dialogue analysis are retained.

E5.justification: The ten GPT judgments per dialogue pair, correlation reporting, and Mann–Whitney U significance conventions remain unchanged. Added comparison rows and human preference percentages do not introduce new seed reporting, repeated-training-run information, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Retained Table 3 results are unchanged, including the original DPO model's 4.87 Overall and 1.75 ES-Intensity scores. V2 adds baseline and Cactus results, target-success rates of 0.720/0.760/0.779 (Table 4), simulator preference rates of 66.4% on ESConv and 33.3% on AnnoMI (Figure 4), and classifier comparisons (Table 6). These are additional findings, not improvements to the original same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The detector and generator mappings and discounted reward equations (1–5) remain unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and the added experiments introduce no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first explicit integration of value reinforcement into emotional-support systems, propose the same two-phase framework, and claim benefits for support quality, emotional relief, and value reinforcement. V2 emphasizes novelty and Reddit knowledge more prominently, while retaining the central contribution and claim scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets Cactus results as evidence of generalizability and attributes Reddit's stronger Experience performance to personal narratives. It also adds a speculative explanation linking GPT-4o's prolonged empathy to human-preference alignment (Sections 6.4.4–6.4.5). These are localized additions; the existing longitudinal and other limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix J documents Cactus intake-form deduplication, selection of 4,057 dialogues, the 11,000/1,631/1,631 data split, and simulation dataset sizes in Table 16. These details mainly support the added variant. Existing hardware, LoRA settings, and prompts are retained, and code/data release remains promised upon publication.

R1.justification: V2 adds the ESCoT reference and two AnnoMI references, and Appendix G explains the relationship to Ask-an-Expert, ESCoT, and PPDPP. Cactus and several newly evaluated methods were already cited in v1. The broader positioning around human values and emotional support remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 revises portions of the abstract and introduction, tightens related-work and results prose, and expands explanations of reference selection and the four-turn analysis window. New experimental subsections and appendices fit within the retained document structure; much existing text remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns Figure 1 to illustrate method inputs and strategy selection, rescales and recaptions Figure 2, and adds the human-evaluation Figure 4 and dedicated experimental tables. Main and appendix comparison tables expand with new comparator categories. Persona examples lose their Value rows. Together these substantially expand and revise the visual presentation of the method and evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important gaps in v1's evaluation through specialist-method comparisons, a 200-dialogue human check of simulator naturalness, direct target-reinforcement measurements, and alternative-source training experiments. These substantially strengthen the empirical support for the framework. Naturalness does not establish real-world or longitudinal effectiveness, and the new preference-alignment explanation remains speculative, but these limitations do not outweigh the gains in validation.
